# Trilayer stacking identification by Fermi-surface counting (ABA vs ABC)

*Investigation — a decision procedure one level up from the measurement recipes
it orchestrates (`measurements/gatemap.md`, `measurements/sdh-spot-check.md`,
`measurements/landau-fan.md`), spanning multiple measurements rather than a single
sweep. Use the rig-appropriate variants; rig and device mechanics — magnet
discipline, gate wiring, validators — live in the device card and session brief,
not here.*

**Reference**: `hera/docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` — the survey that grounds
this recipe, synthesising Datta et al. 2017 (`hera/docs/papers/ncomms14518/paper.md`),
MacDonald et al. 2010 (`hera/docs/papers/1004.1481/paper.md`), and Koshino–McCann
2009 (`hera/docs/papers/0809.0983/paper.md`). Read it first; every band-structure
claim below is grounded there with figure crops you can view.

## What

Classify the stacking order of a trilayer-graphene device — ABA (Bernal) vs ABC
(rhombohedral) — by **counting distinct Fermi surfaces** from Shubnikov–de Haas
frequency content at controlled D ≈ 0, cross-checked by the high-field Landau-level
offset. Output is a **region-resolved, evidence-cited, hedged call**, not a binary.

## When

- A **dual-gated** trilayer device of unknown or unverified stacking is loaded and
  gated, where you can sit at D = 0 and sweep n independently. A single-gated
  device (D ∝ n) uses `trilayer-stacking-id.md` instead.
- Stacking determines everything downstream (ABC hosts the flat-band / correlated
  physics; ABA is conventional), so this is typically among the *first science
  questions* of a trilayer campaign.
- Also worth running when stacking was assigned by optical contrast / Raman only —
  transport is the in-situ check, and trilayer flakes commonly host **mixed
  ABA/ABC domains**, so different contact pairs can disagree. (Reading the Raman
  data itself: `raman-stacking-id.md`; reconciling the two calls:
  `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md`.)

Prerequisites: gates calibrated with validators committed (device-init recipes),
and at least one four-terminal Rxx channel with credible contacts and quantum
mobility high enough to reach SdH onset in the planned field window (Step 3 decides
this). Step 1 handles CNP identification and the (n, D) conversion — a CNP that
cannot be positively identified is itself an outcome to surface, not a precondition.

## Why

The two stackings differ qualitatively in their Fermi-surface count
(`hera/docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` §2–3):

- **ABA**: mirror symmetry → a monolayer-like (ML) Dirac band and a bilayer-like
  (BL) quadratic band coexist → **2 distinct Fermi surfaces** (the ML + BL pair) at
  finite n; each is a single pocket at the ~10¹² operating density.
- **ABC**: a single chiral J = 3 band with a **D-dependent Lifshitz transition at
  low density** (trigonal warping; ~10¹¹ cm⁻², MacDonald), below which the Fermi
  surface reconstructs. Above it — at the ~10¹² operating density — **1 Fermi
  surface**.

**The read is the peak set against the Luttinger frequency, not a headline count.**
F_L = (h/g·e)·n is the density's predicted line — predicted, not fit per peak (g = 4,
spin × valley, while degeneracies are unbroken at low field / warmish T). But its
position inherits the lever-arm **scale** uncertainty (geometry prior, ~10–15% when
the AFM thickness is accurate — `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`), so F_L is
a **band, not a ceiling**: a tone above *nominal* F_L means the scale prior is low,
not that the tone is spurious. Each stacking predicts a distinct *set* of resolved
peaks relative to F_L:

- **ABC**: one tone **at** F_L (the single pocket carries the full density).
- **ABA**: a **pair** partitioning F_L, f_ML + f_BL = F_L. The ML fraction is
  band-structure-dependent and often **small**, so f_BL can sit anywhere from well
  below F_L to nearly at it, and f_ML can be weak.
- **Mixed stacking domains**: the ABC singleton and the ABA pair superposed, each
  grouping checked against the **same** F_L (the domains share the gated density —
  these devices are clean enough that domains do not sit at different densities).
  Peak *amplitudes* track the domains' geometric weighting.
- **A tone at F_L is not automatically ABC**: because the ABA pair sums to F_L, any
  sum tone of the pair — **magnetic breakdown** (a high-B orbit through both pockets,
  F = f_ML + f_BL) or **intermodulation/mixing** — lands exactly at F_L and mimics
  the ABC singleton. A set {f_ML, f_BL, ≈F_L} underdetermines mixed domains;
  discriminate before claiming one (Verify: F_L-tone origin).

So classification is **combinatorial**: enumerate the valid peaks, then match each
subset to a template against F_L. Four disciplines keep it honest:

- **Pin the scale before you reject.** The lever arm is one global number that the
  Luttinger relations pin — an ABC singleton sits at F_L, an ABA pair sums to F_L.
  Fit that single in-band scale to the *whole* peak set *first*, then read tones
  against the refined F_L; a peak is "above F_L" only once the scale is pinned, never
  against the un-pinned prior. More than one population (e.g. mixed domains)
  **over-determines** the scale — leverage, not noise: one scale must satisfy every
  population at once, so pinning off a subset and dropping the rest is wrong. Any
  later scale change is retroactive — re-read the whole set.
- **Classify on frequencies, never amplitudes.** A peak's amplitude folds in field,
  Dingle damping, and domain weighting; it is qualitative at best and never settles
  a count. Frequencies carry the pocket areas — they do the matching.
- **Screen harmonics first.** A real pocket at f throws harmonics at 2f, 3f, … that
  are not pockets; drop any peak at an integer multiple of a stronger fundamental
  (confirm by n-dependence — a harmonic tracks k·f exactly, a real pocket follows
  its own Onsager curve).
- **Read each Rxx channel separately, never averaged.** Each pair probes a region of
  a possibly-mosaic flake: a coherent peak set is a single-domain region, while
  channels that disagree (superposed / incoherent content) flag a stacking mosaic.
  The call is **per region**, and "most channels uninformative" is a normal outcome.

ABA's dominant BL tone nearly coincides with ABC's single tone, so the
discriminating evidence is always the **small ML partner and the partition**, never
the big tone alone.

- **D ≈ 0 is the optimal operating point, and the count is robust to small residual

  global density scale (Why: pin the scale before you reject). Solve the single global
  scale against it before reading any tone as supra-F_L.
- **F_L-tone origin (breakdown | ABC domain | mixing).** For an ABA pair plus a tone
  at ≈F_L: (1) **B-window split** — FFT the low-B and high-B halves separately; a
  breakdown/mixing tone strengthens with B relative to the fundamentals, a real
  pocket keeps its own Dingle envelope (cheap, partial); (2) **grid-change
  reproduction** (`sdh-spot-check.md` Verify) retires the sampling-alias origin;
  (3) the per-branch **LK mass** (below) is decisive. An unresolved remainder is a
  fork to report (STYLE rule 14).
- **LK mass split + beat exclusion** *(our-measurement)*: when two frequencies coexist, the deciding cross-check is a per-branch
  **LK mass** (`temperature-dependence` Flavor B): two distinct masses confirm two
  genuine bands, one mass says one band. Label ML vs BL against model masses at
  E_F, never a light/heavy prior: the ML Dirac mass grows with |n| and can meet
  the BL mass at operating density. Independent exclusion — a **beat** damps with the **sum** of the
  parent masses, so a coexisting component **lighter** than the main branch cannot be
  a beat (decisive); a mass at or above the parents' is consistent-with a beat and
  decides nothing alone.
- **Lever-arm / Nyquist at design time.** Ray slopes / frequencies must quantize
  against the (n, D) calibration; the B-axis SdH period (ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n) sets the
  fan's B-row spacing — a fan that fails the `landau-fan.md` Nyquist check in the
  claim window is uninformative there, re-measure.
- **Domain / mosaic caveat — magnitude is not a clean read.** Under D, a CNP
  resistance that **caps** below MΩ is *consistent-with* small-domain ABC shunted by
  ABA (the channel averages over domains; the ceiling tracks domain size vs channel
  length), **not** evidence against ABC. Feed CNP-vs-D into the per-channel read (Why),
  never as a standalone per-device call (`hera/docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` §5).

## Examples

*(our-measurement — mechanical lessons only.)*

- A per-column SdH-FFT on a fan surfaced frequency structure that (n, B)-plane
  arc-hunting had missed; a slow tone whose n-dependence was
  extraction-window-sensitive was reported as a fork (Verify / STYLE rule 14),
  with the per-branch LK mass as the deciding follow-up.
- A clean single-density `sdh-spot-check` resolved tones a same-session fan —
  run under-settled and at a coarser B-step — did not: the worked case for "a
  noisier fan does not overturn a cleaner spot check" (Verify) and for locking
  acquisition on spot checks before the fan (Step 3).
- Channel facts (current channel + gain division, the Rxx/Rxy pair wiring, glitch
  rows) are device-card / notebook-index data — read them there, never from a recipe
  (STYLE rule 11).

## Next

- **ABA-confirmed** (the ML+BL pair, Luttinger-consistent, Onsager-tracking, distinct
  LK masses): conventional trilayer; campaign value is QHF / interaction physics — needs
  quality and lower T; otherwise deprioritise.
- **ABC-leaning** (single tone on the ABC Onsager curve, D-gap at CNP): the
  interesting outcome — flat-band / correlated candidate. Verify with the D-gap
  systematics (per-channel, domain-aware) and plan the low-T campaign (mK rig) the
  physics deserves.
- **Mixed-domain device**: map which pairs probe which stacking; decide whether any
  single-domain region supports the science goal before more magnet time.
- **Resolution-limited cannot-tell**: state the onset-field / mobility number and what
  side, density, or temperature would change it — a device-quality / rig choice, not
  more sweeps on this rig.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python
# Step 2 (fusion recipe) — spatial registration artifact for vti-01.
# Frame bridges actually available: (a) the three stage-registered video
# images inside vti-01.wip, (b) the device card's topological contact map
# (T_SD -- L1..L4 down one side -- B_SD; R1/R2 dead), (c) the Raman
# contract's regions.npz raster with its inferred device rectangle.
# There is NO GDS and NO post-fab optical image: the flake->finished-device
# link is the piece-identity inference (the 11.5 x 13 um rectangle is the
# only Hall-bar-shaped remnant). Contact positions inside the rectangle are
# unconstrained -> handled as placement variants + jitter, not as one guess.
#
# Run from the run dir:
#   uv run --no-project --with numpy --with matplotlib --with witio \
#       python s1_registration.py
import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap, BoundaryNorm
import witio

RUN = '/data/sharpelab/hera-data/raman-vti-01-20260818-fusion-b'
WIP = f'{RUN}/inputs/vti-01.wip'
NPZ = f'{RUN}/inputs/regions.npz'

proj = witio.read(WIP)
imgs = {}
for cap in ['73474_--Video Image--002', '73474_--Video Image--004',
            '73474_--Video Image--007']:
    d = [x for x in proj.data if (getattr(x, 'caption', '') or '') == cap][0]
    a = d.array()
    gx, gy = d.position_grid()
    imgs[cap[-3:]] = (a, gx, gy)

z = np.load(NPZ)
labels_S0 = z['labels_S0']
labels_S1 = z['labels_S1']
xe, ye = z['x_edges'], z['y_edges']
xc, yc = z['x_centres'], z['y_centres']
rect = json.loads(str(z['device_rect']))
cuts = json.loads(str(z['cut_footprints']))
mapfp = json.loads(str(z['map_footprints']))
RX, RY = rect['x'], rect['y']

# ---- channel placement variants -------------------------------------------
# Hall bar: T_SD -- L1 L2 L3 L4 (probes in order down one side) -- B_SD.
# Channels: sr1 = B_SD-L4, sr2 = L4-L1, sr3 = L3-L2.
# Contacts modeled evenly spaced along the bar axis at fractions 0 (T_SD),
# 1/5..4/5 (L1..L4), 1 (B_SD). Variants: bar axis along y or x, both
# orientations; jitter: rect shifted on a +/-2 um grid (in-frame
# registration budget). Composition counted over classified graphene pixels
# (labels 10/11/12) inside each channel's segment band, full transverse width.
FR = {'sr1': (4/5, 1.0), 'sr2': (1/5, 4/5), 'sr3': (2/5, 3/5)}


def seg_counts(lab, x0, x1, y0, y1, axis, flip, f0, f1):
    if flip:
        f0, f1 = 1 - f1, 1 - f0
    if axis == 'y':
        sy0, sy1 = y0 + f0 * (y1 - y0), y0 + f1 * (y1 - y0)
        sx0, sx1 = x0, x1
    else:
        sx0, sx1 = x0 + f0 * (x1 - x0), x0 + f1 * (x1 - x0)
        sy0, sy1 = y0, y1
    m = ((xc[None, :] >= sx0) & (xc[None, :] <= sx1) &
         (yc[:, None] >= sy0) & (yc[:, None] <= sy1))
    vals = lab[m]
    out = {int(k): int((vals == k).sum()) for k in np.unique(vals)}
    cl = sum(out.get(k, 0) for k in (10, 11, 12))
    return out, cl, out.get(11, 0), out.get(10, 0), out.get(12, 0)


variants = []
for axis in ('y', 'x'):
    for flip in (False, True):
        for dx in (-2, 0, 2):
            for dy in (-2, 0, 2):
                row = {'axis': axis, 'flip': flip, 'dx': dx, 'dy': dy}
                for ch, (f0, f1) in FR.items():
                    out, cl, b, a, mx = seg_counts(
                        labels_S1, RX[0] + dx, RX[1] + dx,
                        RY[0] + dy, RY[1] + dy, axis, flip, f0, f1)
                    row[ch] = {'counts': out, 'classified': cl, 'B_abc': b,
                               'A_aba': a, 'mixed': mx,
                               'abc_frac': (b / cl if cl else None)}
                variants.append(row)

# contract's regions.npz raster with its inferred device rectangle.
# There is NO GDS and NO post-fab optical image: the flake->finished-device
# link is the piece-identity inference (the 11.5 x 13 um rectangle is the
# only Hall-bar-shaped remnant). Contact positions inside the rectangle are
# unconstrained -> handled as placement variants + jitter, not as one guess.
#
# Run from the run dir:
#   uv run --no-project --with numpy --with matplotlib --with witio \
#       python s1_registration.py

WIP = f'{RUN}/inputs/vti-01.wip'
NPZ = f'{RUN}/inputs/regions.npz'

proj = witio.read(WIP)
imgs = {}
for cap in ['73474_--Video Image--002', '73474_--Video Image--004',
            '73474_--Video Image--007']:
    d = [x for x in proj.data if (getattr(x, 'caption', '') or '') == cap][0]
    a = d.array()
    gx, gy = d.position_grid()
    imgs[cap[-3:]] = (a, gx, gy)

z = np.load(NPZ)
labels_S0 = z['labels_S0']
labels_S1 = z['labels_S1']
xe, ye = z['x_edges'], z['y_edges']
xc, yc = z['x_centres'], z['y_centres']
rect = json.loads(str(z['device_rect']))
cuts = json.loads(str(z['cut_footprints']))

# ---- channel placement variants -------------------------------------------
# Hall bar: T_SD -- L1 L2 L3 L4 (probes in order down one side) -- B_SD.
# Channels: sr1 = B_SD-L4, sr2 = L4-L1, sr3 = L3-L2.
# Contacts modeled evenly spaced along the bar axis at fractions 0 (T_SD),
# 1/5..4/5 (L1..L4), 1 (B_SD). Variants: bar axis along y or x, both
# orientations; jitter: rect shifted on a +/-2 um grid (in-frame

    if flip:

        sy0, sy1 = y0 + f0 * (y1 - y0), y0 + f1 * (y1 - y0)
        sx0, sx1 = x0, x1
    else:
        sx0, sx1 = x0 + f0 * (x1 - x0), x0 + f1 * (x1 - x0)
        sy0, sy1 = y0, y1
    m = ((xc[None, :] >= sx0) & (xc[None, :] <= sx1) &
         (yc[:, None] >= sy0) & (yc[:, None] <= sy1))
    vals = lab[m]
    out = {int(k): int((vals == k).sum()) for k in np.unique(vals)}
    cl = sum(out.get(k, 0) for k in (10, 11, 12))
    return out, cl, out.get(11, 0), out.get(10, 0), out.get(12, 0)

                            RY[0] + dy, RY[1] + dy, axis, flip, f0, f1)
                        row[ch] = {'counts': out, 'classified': cl,
                                   'B_abc': b, 'A_aba': a, 'mixed': mx,
                                   'abc_frac': (b / cl if cl else None)}
                    variants.append(row)

              if v[ch]['abc_frac'] is not None]

                       'n_no_coverage': sum(1 for v in variants
                                            if v[ch]['classified'] == 0),
                       'abc_frac_min': float(min(fr)),
                       'abc_frac_max': float(max(fr)),
                       'classified_px_min': int(min(ncl)),

    d = [x for x in proj.data if (getattr(x, 'caption', '') or '') == cap][0]
    a = d.array()
    gx, gy = d.position_grid()
    imgs[cap[-3:]] = (a, gx, gy)

z = np.load(NPZ)
labels_S0 = z['labels_S0']
labels_S1 = z['labels_S1']
xe, ye = z['x_edges'], z['y_edges']
xc, yc = z['x_centres'], z['y_centres']
rect = json.loads(str(z['device_rect']))
cuts = json.loads(str(z['cut_footprints']))
mapfp = json.loads(str(z['map_footprints']))
RX, RY = rect['x'], rect['y']

# ---- channel placement variants -------------------------------------------
# Hall bar: T_SD -- L1 L2 L3 L4 (probes in order down one side) -- B_SD.
# Channels: sr1 = B_SD-L4, sr2 = L4-L1, sr3 = L3-L2.
# Contacts modeled evenly spaced along the bar axis at fractions 0 (T_SD),
# 1/5..4/5 (L1..L4), 1 (B_SD). Variants: bar axis along y or x, both
# orientations; jitter: rect shifted on a +/-2 um grid (in-frame
# registration budget). Composition counted over classified graphene pixels
# (labels 10/11/12) inside each channel's segment band, full transverse width.
FR = {'sr1': (4/5, 1.0), 'sr2': (1/5, 4/5), 'sr3': (2/5, 3/5)}


def seg_counts(lab, x0, x1, y0, y1, axis, flip, f0, f1):
    if flip:
        f0, f1 = 1 - f1, 1 - f0
    if axis == 'y':
        sy0, sy1 = y0 + f0 * (y1 - y0), y0 + f1 * (y1 - y0)
        sx0, sx1 = x0, x1
    else:
        sx0, sx1 = x0 + f0 * (x1 - x0), x0 + f1 * (x1 - x0)
        sy0, sy1 = y0, y1
    m = ((xc[None, :] >= sx0) & (xc[None, :] <= sx1) &
         (yc[:, None] >= sy0) & (yc[:, None] <= sy1))
    vals = lab[m]
    out = {int(k): int((vals == k).sum()) for k in np.unique(vals)}
    cl = sum(out.get(k, 0) for k in (10, 11, 12))
    return out, cl, out.get(11, 0), out.get(10, 0), out.get(12, 0)


def run_grid(jit):
    variants = []
    for axis in ('y', 'x'):
        for flip in (False, True):
            for dx in jit:
                for dy in jit:
                    row = {'axis': axis, 'flip': flip, 'dx': dx, 'dy': dy}
                    for ch, (f0, f1) in FR.items():
                        out, cl, b, a, mx = seg_counts(
                            labels_S1, RX[0] + dx, RX[1] + dx,
                            RY[0] + dy, RY[1] + dy, axis, flip, f0, f1)
                        row[ch] = {'counts': out, 'classified': cl,
                                   'B_abc': b, 'A_aba': a, 'mixed': mx,
                                   'abc_frac': (b / cl if cl else None)}
                    variants.append(row)
    summary = {}
    for ch in FR:
        fr = [v[ch]['abc_frac'] for v in variants
              if v[ch]['abc_frac'] is not None]
        ncl = [v[ch]['classified'] for v in variants]
        summary[ch] = {'n_variants': len(variants),
                       'n_no_coverage': sum(1 for v in variants
                                            if v[ch]['classified'] == 0),
                       'abc_frac_min': float(min(fr)),
                       'abc_frac_max': float(max(fr)),
                       'classified_px_min': int(min(ncl)),
                       'classified_px_max': int(max(ncl))}
    return variants, summary

variants2, summary2 = run_grid((-2, 0, 2))         # stress margin

whole = {}
for tag, lab in (('S0', labels_S0), ('S1', labels_S1)):
    out, cl, b, a, mx = seg_counts(lab, RX[0], RX[1], RY[0], RY[1], 'y', False, 0, 1)
    whole[tag] = {'counts': out, 'classified': cl, 'B_abc': b, 'A_aba': a,
                  'mixed': mx, 'abc_frac': b / cl if cl else None}

with open(f'{RUN}/intermediates/registration_coverage.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump({'device_rect': rect, 'cut_footprints': cuts,
               'contact_fractions': FR, 'whole_rect': whole,
               'variant_summary_pm1um': summary,
               'variant_summary_pm2um_stress': summary2,
               'variants_pm1um': variants,
               'variants_pm2um_stress': variants2}, f, indent=1)

# ---- figure ---------------------------------------------------------------
lab_colors = {0: (1, 1, 1, 0), 1: (.92, .92, .92, .6), 2: (.35, .35, .35, .8),
              3: (.75, .75, .95, .8), 5: (.85, .85, .6, .7),
              10: (.10, .45, .85, .75), 11: (.90, .35, .10, .75),
              12: (.55, .10, .60, .8)}
keys = sorted(lab_colors)                      # [0,1,2,3,5,10,11,12]
cmap = ListedColormap([lab_colors[k] for k in keys])
norm = BoundaryNorm([-.5, .5, 1.5, 2.5, 4, 7.5, 10.5, 11.5, 12.5], len(keys))


def show_img(ax, key, ds=4):
    a, gx, gy = imgs[key]
    ax.pcolormesh(gx[::ds, ::ds], gy[::ds, ::ds],
                  a[::ds, ::ds].mean(axis=2)[:-1, :-1] if False else
                  a[::ds, ::ds, :].mean(axis=2), cmap='gray', shading='auto',
                  rasterized=True)


def show_labels(ax, lab, alpha=1.0):
    ax.pcolormesh(xe, ye, lab, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, shading='flat',
                  alpha=alpha, rasterized=True)


def draw_rect(ax, x, y, **kw):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x[0], y[0]), x[1] - x[0], y[1] - y[0],
                           fill=False, **kw))


fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 11))
for ax in axs.flat:
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.set_xlabel('stage x (µm)')
    ax.set_ylabel('stage y (µm)')

ax = axs[0, 0]
show_img(ax, '002')
show_labels(ax, labels_S0, alpha=.5)
draw_rect(ax, RX, RY, ec='lime', lw=2)
draw_rect(ax, mapfp['22'][:2], mapfp['22'][2:], ec='w', lw=1, ls='--')
ax.set_xlim(-12085, -12020); ax.set_ylim(1260, 1308)
ax.set_title('S0 12:55–12:57 — video 002 + map-22 labels\n'
             'orange=B/ABC, blue=A/ABA, purple=wall; green=inferred device rect')

ax = axs[0, 1]
show_img(ax, '004')
show_labels(ax, labels_S1, alpha=.5)
draw_rect(ax, RX, RY, ec='lime', lw=2)
draw_rect(ax, mapfp['27'][:2], mapfp['27'][2:], ec='w', lw=1, ls='--')
for k, c in cuts.items():
    draw_rect(ax, c['x'], c['y'], ec='red', lw=1.5, ls=':')
ax.set_xlim(-12060, -12020); ax.set_ylim(1260, 1305)
ax.set_title('S1 13:19–13:20 — video 004 + map-27 labels\n'
             'red dotted = later 1064 nm cut passes (13:27 / 13:30)')

ax = axs[1, 0]
show_img(ax, '007')
draw_rect(ax, RX, RY, ec='lime', lw=2)
for k, c in cuts.items():
    draw_rect(ax, c['x'], c['y'], ec='red', lw=1.5, ls=':')
# channel schematic, axis=y variant, T_SD at top (y1) — TOPOLOGICAL ONLY
x_bar = (RX[0] + RX[1]) / 2
names = ['B_SD', 'L4', 'L3', 'L2', 'L1', 'T_SD']
for i, nm in enumerate(names):
    yy = RY[0] + i / 5 * (RY[1] - RY[0])
    ax.plot([RX[0], RX[1]], [yy, yy], color='cyan', lw=.8, ls='--')
    ax.text(RX[1] + .4, yy, nm, color='cyan', fontsize=8, va='center')
for ch, (f0, f1), off in [('sr1', FR['sr1'], -3.2), ('sr2', FR['sr2'], -4.4),
                          ('sr3', FR['sr3'], -5.6)]:
    y0 = RY[0] + (1 - f1) * (RY[1] - RY[0])
    y1 = RY[0] + (1 - f0) * (RY[1] - RY[0])
    ax.plot([RX[0] + off + 1.2] * 2, [y0, y1], lw=3)
    ax.text(RX[0] + off + .6, (y0 + y1) / 2, ch, fontsize=9, va='center',
            ha='right', color='k')
ax.set_xlim(-12060, -12020); ax.set_ylim(1260, 1300)
ax.set_title('post-cut video 007 (13:29) + one placement variant\n'
             'contact positions NOT registered — evenly-spaced model, all variants stress-tested')

ax = axs[1, 1]
show_labels(ax, labels_S1, alpha=1)
draw_rect(ax, RX, RY, ec='lime', lw=2)
for k, c in cuts.items():
    draw_rect(ax, c['x'], c['y'], ec='red', lw=1.5, ls=':')
txt = [f"whole rect S1: {whole['S1']['B_abc']}/{whole['S1']['classified']} "
       f"classified px ABC ({100*whole['S1']['abc_frac']:.0f}%)"]
for ch in ('sr1', 'sr2', 'sr3'):
    s = summary[ch]
    txt.append(f"{ch}: ABC share {100*s['abc_frac_min']:.0f}–"
               f"{100*s['abc_frac_max']:.0f}% over {s['n_variants']} variants")
ax.text(.02, .02, '\n'.join(txt), transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9,

ax.set_xlim(-12052, -12028); ax.set_ylim(1262, 1300)
ax.set_title('S1 labels, device-rect zoom — coverage stress result')

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f'{RUN}/figures/f_registration.png', dpi=160)
print(json.dumps({'whole_rect': whole, 'variant_summary': summary}, indent=1))

# vti-01 fusion — Step 2 registration artifact (binding)

Produced by `s1_registration.py` (this dir); figure
`figures/f_registration.png`; numbers `intermediates/registration_coverage.json`.
Coordinate frame: **WITec stage µm of `inputs/vti-01.wip`** (sample `73474_`,
2026-05-28) — the Raman contract's frame, carried by `inputs/regions.npz`
(`x_edges`/`y_edges`, 1 µm pitch).

## Frame bridges used (the complete set supplied)

1. **In-file stage-registered video images** 002 (12:55, pre-cut), 004
   (13:19, post-first-cut), 007 (13:29, post-1064 nm top pass) — extracted
   with `witio`, per-pixel stage-µm position grids from the in-file space
   transformations. These tie video ↔ both Raman maps exactly (metadata-level).
2. **Device card contact map** — topology only: Hall bar, `T_SD` and `B_SD`
   at the two ends, `L1…L4` voltage probes in order down one side, `R1/R2`
   dead. Channels: sr1 = B_SD–L4, sr2 = L4–L1, sr3 = L3–L2. **No physical
   pad geometry** (pad numbers are breakout wiring, not positions).
3. **Ana notebook geometry** — parsed (JSON); contains only gate-stack
   thicknesses. **No channel dimensions or probe spacings.**

Not supplied: GDS, post-fab optical image, build-step list. The
flake-frame → finished-device link therefore rests on **one inferred anchor**:
the device rectangle x −12045.5…−12034, y 1274…1287 µm (11.5 × 13 µm), the
only Hall-bar-shaped remnant after the cuts (Raman contract Step 0 inference,
carried verbatim in `regions.npz:device_rect` — not testimony).

## Channel placement model

Contact positions inside the rectangle are unregistered. Model: SD contacts
at the two ends of the bar axis, L1…L4 evenly spaced between (fractions
1/5…4/5); segment bands at full transverse width. **36 variants** = bar axis
along y or x × both orientations × rectangle jitter on a ±1 µm grid (the
stated in-frame uncertainty). A ±2 µm grid is run as stress margin.

## Registration uncertainty vs domain scale

| link | uncertainty | basis |
|---|---|---|
| map 22 ↔ map 27 ↔ video | ≤ 1 µm | in-file transforms; S0↔S1 best integer shift (0,0) µm, label agreement 92% (Raman contract) |
| map pixel ↔ true stage (wall positions) | ±1 µm | 1 µm step, 0.7 µm spot; scan rotation 0.5° ≲ 0.15 µm across the rect |
| rectangle edges ↔ piece (imagery) | ±1 µm | video pixel 49 nm; cut-kerf edge reading |
| **combined in-frame** | **±1 µm (stress ±2 µm)** | — |
| contact positions inside rect | unconstrained | handled as the 36 placement variants, not a µm number |
| **flake frame ↔ finished device (piece identity)** | **not a µm number — an inference** | anchor-variant B below |

Domain scale: the ABC lobe (region B) main component is ~25 × 30 µm, walls
1–2 µm; the rectangle interior is a **single 238-px connected ABC component**
at S1. In-frame uncertainty (±1 µm) ≪ domain scale, so coverage labels are
stable against it — the binding uncertainty is the piece-identity anchor,
which is all-or-nothing, and the sub-spot/sub-µm blindness inherited from
the Raman contract.

## Coverage classification (S1 = map 27, the last pre-processing view)

Whole rectangle: S0 149/156 classified px ABC (96%); S1 **123/127 ABC (97%)**,
1 ABA px, 3 wall px. The only coherent ABA structure (18-px strip at the
slanted top, y 1290–1295) lies **outside** the rectangle, inside the 13:27
cut footprint, and is gone from the final piece.

| channel | coverage | ABC share of classified px (36 variants, ±1 µm) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| sr1 (B_SD–L4) | **partial** (registration-limited) | 88–100% where covered; **3/36 variants: no classified coverage** (bar-along-x placements put the end segment on map-27's partial-spot right-edge column) | end-segment band also abuts the rectangle's bottom edge = 13:30 1064 nm pass margin (post-S1, unobserved) |
| sr2 (L4–L1) | **covered** | 96–100% (69–91 px in every variant) | |
| sr3 (L3–L2) | **covered** | 92–100% (26–33 px in every variant) | |

±2 µm stress margin: sr1 88–100% (3/36 no-coverage), sr2 95–100%, sr3
92–100% — no label changes beyond sr1's existing partial status.

**Anchor-variant B (piece identity fails):** if the rectangle is not the
piece that became vti-01, all three channels are **uncovered** — no
interpolation; each row degrades to single-modality (transport). Recorded in
the stress audit; there is no second in-frame anchor to fit against, so this
is a discrete variant, not a spread.

All coverage is **as of S1 (2026-05-28 13:20)** — contact metal deposition
moves stacking walls by µm (base-recipe converter list), so even "covered"
does not pin the *measurement-time* domain composition; that is the Step 3
temporal gap, not a registration defect.

# vti-01 — fused Raman × transport stacking verdict

Recipe: `hera/recipes/investigations/stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md`.
Inputs: locked transport call (`inputs/transport-call.md`, ana cells 33 + 38
verified verbatim-consistent by parse), locked Raman contract
(`inputs/raman-contract.md` + `inputs/raman-provenance.md` +
`inputs/regions.npz`, `.wip` sha256 verified `5b5ffe6b…8434`), device card,
session notes, `inputs/vti-01.wip`.
Registration artifact (binding): **`registration.md`** +
`figures/f_registration.png` + `intermediates/registration_coverage.json`,
regenerated by `s1_registration.py`.

## Step 1 — admissibility + independence

Both contracts admissible: weight words, evidence lists, coordinates present.
Transport: per-channel (sr1 = B_SD–L4, sr2 = L4–L1, sr3 = L3–L2), runs cited,
(n, D) coordinates, calibration provenance. Raman: stage-µm regions **with the
label raster** (`regions.npz`) and stage stamps S0/S1 — no prose-only
re-derivation needed.

**Independence audit — pass.** The Raman provenance line states no transport
result, notebook, session note, or third-party view was received. The
transport-side inputs (call, ana notebook, session notes, device card as of
the call) contain no Raman/WITec reference (full-text scan; the only "532"
hits are numeric coincidences inside base64 payloads). The calls were
produced in separate sessions from disjoint evidence. Fusion is evidential.

## Step 2 — spatial registration (see `registration.md`)

One frame: WITec stage µm. Anchors: in-file stage-registered video images
(exact), device-card contact topology, and the inferred device rectangle
x −12045.5…−12034, y 1274…1287 µm — the piece-identity link is an
**inference, not testimony** (no GDS, no post-fab image supplied).
In-frame uncertainty **±1 µm** (stress ±2 µm) against a domain scale of
~25–30 µm with the rectangle interior a single 238-px ABC component —
uncertainty ≪ domain scale. Contact positions inside the rectangle are
unregistered → 36 placement variants stress-tested.

Coverage (as of S1): **sr2 covered** (ABC 96–100% of classified px in every
variant), **sr3 covered** (92–100%), **sr1 partial** — registration-limited:
88–100% ABC where covered, but 3/36 variants (bar-axis-along-x placements)
put its end segment on map-27's unclassified right-edge column. Uncovered
stays uncovered — no interpolation.

## Step 3 — temporal registration

Raman stage stamp S1 = 2026-05-28 13:20 (imagery-inferred); transport
measured 2026-08-18→20. Intervening steps, by conversion risk
(ABC→ABA direction only; all undated, no testimony):

| step | risk class | evidence status |
|---|---|---|
| first laser cut (12:57→13:19) | clean thermal, local | **bracketed by S0→S1 differencing** (like-conditioned: both bare-flake, through-stack screen not triggered): label agreement 92%, no conversion inside the rectangle |
| 1064 nm cut passes 13:27/13:30 | clean thermal, locally far above conversion threshold | after S1 — rectangle's top 0–1 µm and bottom 0–2 µm margins inside the pass footprints, unobserved after |
| hBN pickup / encapsulation | transfer–pickup (armchair pickup converts ABC→ABA) | inferred from device description; undated |
| dual-gate stack assembly (graphite BG) | transfer–pickup | inferred; undated |
| **contact metal deposition** | **highest — walls move by µm** | inferred (finished Hall bar has metal contacts); undated |
| any anneal/bake | chemical + bake | unknown; undated |

No later-stage map exists, so everything after S1 is risk-class inference,
not differenced evidence. The gate-clean S1 map carries the buried-channel
call.

## Step 4 — per-region fusion

| channel | transport verdict + strength | Raman verdict + strength + stage | fused verdict + strength | mechanism class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **sr1** (B_SD–L4) | ABA / Bernal (**strong, two-branch**: f_BL + f_ML resolved, Luttinger closes at λ = 1.14, masses pin identities) | ABC (**strong**) as of S1 2026-05-28 13:20; coverage **partial** (88–100% ABC where covered) | **ABA (strong)** at measurement time; region recorded **"converted (consistent-with), steps: contact metal deposition / hBN pickup–encapsulation (+ 1064 nm cut margins), undated"** | **Reconciled-by-conversion** (33/36 registration variants; the 3 no-coverage variants give single-modality-transport with the **same fused verdict** — class registration-limited, verdict stable) |
